newsitem.title: CROATIA: SOCCER-INJURY-PLAGUED CROATIA MUST WIN, SAYS BOBAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURY-PLAGUED CROATIA MUST WIN, SAYS BOBAN.

text.p: Croatia's captain Zvonimir Boban on Friday called on the fanatic Split crowd to lift his injury-plagued team to victory in a crucial World Cup qualifier against Denmark on Saturday.
"It is obvious that this is not the best possible moment for many players, but a victory is a must," Boban, who plays in Italy for AC Milan, told the sports daily Sportske Novosti.
"I expect full support from the crowd," said Boban, who rated his team's chances of victory at 60-40. "We are a better team after all, we should win."

Croatia drew 1-1 against Greece in Zagreb, and now need to beat both Denmark on Saturday, and Slovenia four days later in order to qualify for the 1998 World Cup finals in France from a relatively weak group.
Some of the key players from the team that beat Denmark 3-0 last summer at the European championship in England have come to Split unfit or injured.

Coach Miroslav Blazevic was reportedly considering dropping central defender Nikola Jerkan who has spent much of the past season on the Nottingham Forest bench, but an injury to another defender, Igor Stimac of Derby County, forced him to change his mind.
"Since we lost Stimac, we cannot make any further changes to the last line, so Jerkan will therefore most probably keep his place in the libero position," Blazevic was quoted as saying.
Zvonimir Soldo, who has been in great form for Bundesliga title contenders Vfb Stuttgart, was tipped to replace Stimac as the second stopper.

But Blazevic's main problem is down the right side, where he previously used versatile and agile Mario Stanic of Italian side Parma. Stanic was perhaps the fittest player in the team before hurting his knee on Wednesday.
His place will be filled by either pacy full-back Niko Kovac of German first division Bayer Leverkusen, or, in a more defensive role, Dario Simic of Croatia Zagreb.
Croatia's attack looks quite clear -- Davor Suker of Real Madrid and Alen Boksic of world champions Juventus make a dream striking pair.
In midfield, Blazevic is expected to cast a standard quartet of Boban, Aljosa Asanovic, Robert Jarni and Robert Prosinecki.
Probable lineup: Drazen Ladic, Nikola Jerkan, Zvonimir Soldo, Slaven Bilic, Niko Kovac (Dario Simic), Robert Jarni, Robert Prosinecki, Aljosa Asanovic, Zvonimir Boban, Davor Suker, Alen Boskic.
